Tapestry
Tapestry Online Learning Journal – Parents’ Guide Introduction
All of our children have a personal on-line Learning Journal which records photos, observations and comments, in line with the Early Years Foundation Stage/National Curriculum. This builds up a record of your child’s experiences during their time with us.
We use Tapestry, a system, which is hosted on secure servers in the EU. You will have secure access (via email address and password) to your child’s Learning Journal and, in addition to viewing our contributions, we encourage you to add to it by uploading photos and comments of your child’s learning at home.
We will set up an account for you with the email address we have on our records. You will receive an email from Tapestry with your log in details. Once you have set yourself a password and PIN from the activation email, please go to https://tapestryjournal.com on your computer and log into your Tapestry account. You are also able to download the Tapestry App for different devices. If you have an iPhone or iPad, visit the iTunes store and download the Tapestry app from the Education section (search for Tapestry) or if you have an android device, then you may download the android app from the Google Play Store.
Changing your settings
On the computer At the top right of your screen you will see your name, and selecting this will give you the option to ‘Edit Preferences’. Choose this option and you will be presented with a screen giving you the option to change your email address and password. You also have the option to receive an email whenever a new observation is added to your child’s Learning Journey – just tick or untick the relevant box if you would like to change this setting. On iPhone/iPad To change your settings on the iPhone/iPad app, click the 'cog' button on the bottom right hand side of the application. This enables you to change password and/or email address. Viewing my child’s Learning Journey Once logged in, you will see your child’s observations on your home screen in a list – selecting any one of these will open up the observation for you to look at.
Adding an entry to my child’s Learning Journey
Choose the ‘Add Observation’ option (or the 'plus' icon on your iPhone/iPad) and add the relevant information in the boxes on screen. Photos and videos may be uploaded by choosing the ‘add media’ option. When you have saved your observation, you may go back to the home screen at any time by choosing ‘home’. Remember

pageCache.pageTitle: Priory Infant School, CT11 - Curriculum Intent, Implementation and Impact
pageCache.text:
Curriculum intent, implementation and impact
At Priory Infant School we want all our children to be confident learners who enjoy coming to school and who develop a love and thirst for learning during their time with us from Reception to the end of Year 2.
In their Reception year the children work towards achieving their Early Learning Goals in 7 key areas through continuous provision and active indoor and outdoor play. Early essential skills in phonics, reading, writing, speaking and listening and maths are practised and developed in readiness for the children moving into Year 1 and the Key Stage 1 National Curriculum.
Progression of the skills and knowledge for each subject area are mapped out so that it is clear what the children will learn in each year group and to ensure all National Curriculum objectives are covered before the children move onto their junior school and into Key Stage 2.
Within the curriculum we develop children’s understanding of British Values as well as their personal, social, moral, cultural and health and relationships education. We are passionate in broadening children’s experiences and curriculum opportunities above and beyond the National Curriculum, with our pupils working towards achieving the ‘50 Priory Things’ in their ‘Passport of Fun’ which we truly believe develops the whole child and fosters a greater creative and adventurous side to their learning and development.
How this is Implemented
In order to achieve our aims we teach the curriculum through subject areas. Teachers make connections with children’s prior learning, enable cross- curricular links, enrich vocabulary and teach using explanation, modelling, scaffolding and practice.
The curriculum is differentiated where necessary in order to address the needs of all our pupils and repetition is fundamental, especially in the core subject areas, to enable children to consolidate and build upon their knowledge, skills and understanding.
We recognise the importance and benefit of providing wider opportunities and experiences and engage in local community projects such as Artsmark and Eco Schools. Visitors and experts are invited into school to inspire and engage our children and provide opportunities that they may not otherwise experience. Educational visits and trips are organised to broaden aspirations and provide further memorable learning experiences.
During Reception the children work towards developing characteristics of effective learning. We build effective partnerships with parents as we recognise the importance of the collaboration between school and home. Parents are kept well informed of what their child is learning and how this can be supported and consolidated at home.
Phonics is taught using the ‘Letters and Sounds’ programme to ensure consistency across the year groups with children assessed towards the end of Year 1 using the Phonics Screening Check.
By the time our pupils leave Priory Infant School at the end of Year 2, they are equipped with the skills and knowledge necessary to begin the next stage of their education. They have developed independence in their learning and are resilient to challenges, problem solving and change.
In the Reception classes, Tapestry, an online learning journal, will have tracked coverage of the depth of each pupil’s knowledge, skills and understanding in all key areas. Across the other year groups the children’s progress in all subjects will have been assessed regularly, both formally and informally, using retrieval practice methods such as quizzes or questioning; as well as observations and book looks.
To ensure our children are improving their fluency and mastery and are on track in their learning and development pupil progress is monitored termly. This enables the support or intervention for any children not making expected progress to be put into place swiftly to address individual pupil’s needs.
Teacher assessment in reading, writing and maths is reported to parents every year and the school compares this with national data.

Personal, Social and Health Education
At Priory Infant School we seek to provide a safe, secure learning environment for PSHE that enables children to gain accurate knowledge, develop their own values and attitudes, and develop skills to grow into happy confident successful adults. Our aim is to develop the “whole child”, which includes intellectual, physical, aesthetic and spiritual development. This is the basis of the school’s curriculum, but underlying this is each child’s emotional, moral and social development.
Our PSHE and citizenship curriculum enables children to become healthy, responsible, independent members of society. We purposely adopt a practical and play-based approach to PSHE topics and involve drama and role play as much as possible, believing this to be the best way forward for young children to explore the issues involved. All staff at Priory Infant School are aware of the need to develop these aspects whenever the opportunity arises. We aim to encourage each child to develop as an individual and grow in confidence as they learn to deal with and cope with the more difficult emotional experiences of life. We encourage each child to respect other children and adults and be sensitive to their views even if they differ from their own. We promote the need to consider the thoughts and feelings of others and try to build a good relationship with them. We help each child understand the need for authority and to adhere to rules.
The PSHE curriculum focuses on 5 core strands:
1. Families and Relationships
2. Health and Wellbeing
3. Safety and the Changing Body
5. Economic Wellbeing

pageCache.text:
Desert Class Learning Showcase
2025-2026
Term 5 Highlights
Year 2 have had a busy and enjoyable term filled with exciting learning opportunities. We explored different beliefs and values, learning about how people show care and respect for others and the world around them. In History, we learned about the monarchy and castles, discovering how they have shaped life in Britain over time.
We enjoyed getting creative through our art work with clay and were inspired by the work of artist Rachel Whiteread. In English, Toys in Space sparked our imaginations and helped us create a range of exciting writing. In Maths, we developed our understanding of measurement, time and fractions through practical activities and problem-solving.
Our Science learning focused on plants, where we investigated what seeds need to grow and explored plant life cycles. We also enjoyed learning about the International Space Station in Computing.
Alongside our classroom learning, we took part in trips, music experiences and sporting activities, developing our teamwork, confidence and independence. We are incredibly proud of all the effort and enthusiasm the children have shown throughout the term.
Year 2 Term 5 Highlights
Term 4 Highlights
This term in Year 2, the children have enjoyed a broad and engaging curriculum, enriched by exciting events such as World Book Day, British Science Week and our whole-school PSHE Day. In English, they explored high-quality texts including Tadpole’s Promise and If All the World Were… developing their writing through sequencing events, using time adverbials and retelling stories with their own creative ideas. In Maths, the children built confidence with multiplication and division, before moving on to measuring length and height using standard units. In Science, they learned about lifecycles, including observing changes in frog spawn over time, and explored the importance of health and exercise. In History, they discovered the achievements of the Wright Brothers and the history of flight, while in RE they explored celebrations such as Easter and Eid. The children also developed their computing skills through coding and debugging, and in DT they designed and created their own fairground models using mechanisms. In PE, they built their skills in handball and dance, improving their coordination, control and teamwork.
Term 4 Highlights Y2
Term 3 Highlights
This term, we have enjoyed a wide range of exciting learning across the curriculum. In English, we explored The Bear and the Piano, developing our writing in the first person and using past tense and contractions. In maths, we built on our knowledge of 2D and 3D shapes, explored their properties and began learning about money. Our science learning focused on materials and their uses, while in geography we learnt about our wonderful world and both human and physical features. In RE, we explored the Jewish faith, and in art we experimented with colour, texture and different media. We also took part in a whole-school PSHE day focused on being brave and trying new things, enjoyed music from around the UK, and developed our balance, co-ordination and confidence in PE and swimming.
Year 2 Term 3
Term 2 Highlights
This term in English, we began with Jim and the Beanstalk by Raymond Briggs, where the children discovered a giant beanstalk in the classroom! This inspired lots of creative writing, including making predictions and writing our own fairy tale sequels. We then read the exciting book Wolves by Emily Gravett and even met a wolf expert, Red Riding Hood, who helped us learn that not all books are factual. This supported our understanding of the difference between fact and fiction and the key features of information texts, leading to the children writing factual sentences about wolves. In Science, we explored microhabitats through a bug hunt around the school grounds and by making a wormery. In Sport, we developed our skills in tennis and dodgeball. In History, we learned about how schools have changed over time by comparing schools past and present, and we also marked Remembrance with a special focus on the role of animals in war.
Year 2 Term 2 Highlights 2025
Term 1 Highlights
What a fantastic term of learning and discovery it’s been! 🌟
In English, the children have been inspired by The Journey Home by Frann Preston-Gannon. Through this powerful story, they’ve explored themes of conservation and learnt about the challenges endangered animals face around the world. The children have created fact files about endangered species and written persuasive pieces about why we need to protect them. Along the way, they’ve been learning to identify different types of sentences — questions, commands, statements, and exclamations — and have practised editing their work carefully, thinking about tense, word choice, and word classes such as nouns, verbs, and adjectives. 🐘🐧🌍
In Maths, we’ve been building on our understanding of place value with numbers to 100. The children have enjoyed lots of practical activities to help them compare, order, and represent numbers in different ways. 🔢✨
In Science, we’ve been learning about habitats. The children explored our school’s wildlife area to observe living things in their local environment and then followed up their learning with a fantastic trip to Monkton Nature Reserve, where they discovered even more about how animals and plants survive and thrive in their natural habitats. 🐛🌿🦋
In Geography, we’ve been finding out about hot and cold places around the world. The children have compared different climates, explored where animals live, and discussed how people adapt to life in very different environments. ❄️☀️🌎
It’s been a brilliant term full of curiosity, creativity, and care for our planet — we’re so proud of all the children’s enthusiasm and hard work! 🌿💫

Music
Music is an important aspect of a young child’s life and we endeavour to develop their experience through a range of musical activities.
Every child has an opportunity to experience a wide variety of music through listening, composing and performing. We have an extensive range of percussion instruments and musical resources for all children to use and we follow the exciting Oaks academy music scheme.
Children love to perform both during class time and on stage in the playground, and we plan in opportunities for them to learn to sing, perform rhymes, songs and routines as they take part in annual Christmas Productions and events throughout the school year.
As a school we integrate music within the Zones of Regulation and in our Nurture group using resources such as minuteoflistening.com. We aim to make music accessible and inclusive to all at Priory where each student’s budding talent is cultivated and for music to be enjoyed throughout the school year.

All Local Authority maintained schools in England have a governing body which have three major responsibilities:
At Priory, our governing body follows the circle model of governance and is made up of the Headteacher and volunteers representing staff, parents, the local authority, and the local community. A key part of the role is to act as a ‘critical friend’. This means that we support the Headteacher and other staff but also challenge and ask questions.
We work closely with the Headteacher, staff and the local authority to ensure the school functions well and maintains the proper range of academic and social objectives.

Our SENCO
My name is Mrs. Joyner, and I’m proud to be the SENCO here at Priory. At our school, we believe that every child is unique and full of potential. My role is to ensure that all children with additional needs are supported, valued, and given every opportunity to thrive in a happy, inclusive environment.
We know that the early years of education are incredibly important, and we are committed to working closely with parents and carers to provide the very best support from the very start. Whether your child has an identified need or you’re seeking advice and reassurance, please know we are here to help.
The SEND pages offers some information about how we support children with SEND at Priory Infant School, along with useful resources. If you have any questions or would like to speak to me directly, please do not hesitate to get in contact.
Together, we can help your child grow with confidence, kindness, and joy.

Phonics
At Priory we follow the 'Little Wandle Letters and Sounds' revised programme.
Phonics is a way of teaching children how to read and write. It helps children hear, identify and use different sounds that distinguish one word from another in the English language.Written language can be compared to a code, so knowing the sounds of individual letters and how those letters sound when they’re combined will help children decode words as they read.
Understanding phonics will also help children know which letters to use when they are writing words.
Phonics involves matching the sounds of spoken English with individual letters or groups of letters. For example, the sound k can be spelled as c, k, ck or ch.
Teaching children to blend the sounds of letters together helps them decode unfamiliar or unknown words by sounding them out. For example, when a child is taught the sounds for the letters t, p, a and s, they can start to build up the words: “tap”, “taps”, “pat”, “pats” and “sat”.
